newsitem.title: USA: USDA unswayed by lawmaker appeal for more CRP land.
newsitem.headline: USDA unswayed by lawmaker appeal for more CRP land.

text.p: Agriuclture Department officials said Wednesday they would consider a request to put three million more acres into the Conservation Reserve but one noted USDA never took such a unilateral step in the past.
"We're going to take this letter and their request under consideration," Dallas Smith, acting agriculture undersecretary, told reporters.

Parks Shackleford, a Farm Service Agency official, said, "I don't recall us going back and doing that" when asked if USDA had altered the results of earlier "sign-ups" for the Conservation Reserve Program.

Last month, USDA said it would accept 16.1 million acres out of more than 25 million offered for CRP. Some farm-state lawmakers criticized the decision, saying USDA should accept the maximum amount of acreage possible
In a letter Tuesday, four dozen lawmakers asked USDA to revise its May decision and enroll an additional three million acres.

During a House Agrculture subcommittee hearing, Smith said the 16.1 million acres represented the greatest environmental benefits at the lowest cost. Another CRP signup will be offered in the fall, he said.
